active_chlorine_generation.value: no generation of active chlorine species

nodes.source_text: To demonstrate that selective oxygen production under ultra-high current densities, a commercial active chlorine detector was used to detect the electrolyte after the CP test at 2 A cm−2. As shown in Figure S13, there is no generation of active chlorine species during the process, which demonstrated the selectivity of OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS analysis shows Fe 2p peaks at 706.9 and 719.8 eV corresponding to Fe²⁺, and Co 2p peaks at 780.6 and 796.5 eV corresponding to Co²⁺, confirming oxidation states in K₂[CoFe(CN)₆].
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of Fe 2p (Figure S3a) shows a pair of peaks located at 706.9 and 719.8 eV, corresponding to Fe²⁺ 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ spin orbitals, respectively. While the peaks centered at 780.6 and 796.5 eV in Figure S3b are ascribed to the 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ of Co²⁺...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM imaging reveals cap-pin structure of CoFePBA/Co₂P composite with clear morphological distinction between ferricyanide caps and phosphide pins.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the cap-pin structure can be observed clearly from the transmission electron microscope (TEM) image (inset of Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM imaging shows morphological evolution from nanopins (Co₂P) to caps (CoFePBA) structure in the composite electrode.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Along with the structural evolution from phosphide to ferricyanide, a change in morphology is seen from nanopins (Co₂P, Figure S4a) to caps (Figure 1d and Figure S4b, CoFePBA).

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping shows uniform dispersion of Fe(CN)₆³⁻, CN⁻, PO₄³⁻, and PO₃⁻ species on the electrode surface, with Fe(CN)₆³⁻ covering the surface of Co₂P pins.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the Time of Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) mapping and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping are utilized, which show that Co, Fe, P, N, C, and K elements are uniformly dispersed over the whole sample (Figure 1e and Figure S5). It can be seen that only the Fe(CN)₆³⁻ covers the surface of the electrode...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co, Fe, and P elements throughout the CoFePBA/Co₂P composite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the Time of Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) mapping and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping are utilized, which show that Co, Fe, P, N, C, and K elements are uniformly dispersed over the whole sample (Figure 1e and Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry in 1 M NaOH + 0.5 M NaCl shows CoFePBA/Co₂P with lowest overpotential of 257 mV at 10 mA/cm² and 297 mV at 100 mA/cm², and lowest Tafel slope of 43.5 mV/dec.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, CoFePBA/Co₂P exhibit the lowest overpotential of 257 mV and 297 mV, respectively, to achieve the current density of 10 (η₁₀) and 100 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀₀), respectively... the CoFePBA/Co₂P sample shows the lowest Tafel slope of 43.5 mV dec⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry in 20 wt% NaOH + saturated NaCl shows CoFePBA/Co₂P with overpotential η₁₀ = 246 mV and ultra-low Tafel slope of 31.0 mV/dec.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CoFePBA/Co₂P electrode shows a much lower overpotential (η₁₀ = 246 mV) and ultra-low Tafel slope (Figure S6d, 31.0 mV dec⁻¹) than the other samples...

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows CoFePBA/Co₂P has much lower Ohmic resistance and charge transfer resistance compared to CoFePBA due to the highly conductive Co₂P layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen from the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and the corresponding fitting results (Figure S7 and Table S1), the Ohmic resistance and charge transfer resistance of CoFePBA/Co₂P is much lower than that of CoFePBA, which is due to the presence of highly conductive layer of Co₂P-pins.

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronopotentiometry at 200 mA/cm² in 20 wt% NaOH + saturated NaCl shows CoFePBA/Co₂P maintains excellent stability over 1000 hours with no corrosion or performance attenuation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CP tests were further performed at the industrially relevant current density (200 mA cm⁻²) to simulate the continuous saline water electrolysis process. As can be seen from Figure 2c, the CoFePBA, Co₂P, and Co(OH)₂ electrodes exhibit lose in stability within 100 h due to corrosion by high concentrations of Cl⁻. In stark contrast, CoFePBA/Co₂P show excellent stability and performance, and even improvement after 1000 h operation...

Similar results were obtained from tests in real seawater at high current densities (1 A cm⁻², Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy at potentials from OCP to 1.8 V vs RHE in 20 wt% NaOH + saturated NaCl shows Co-O vibration peaks at 400-600 cm⁻¹ indicating (Co,Fe)-OOH formation, stable -CN- peaks at 2000-2200 cm⁻¹, and PO₄³⁻ peaks at 900-1100 cm⁻¹ appearing at 1.4 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An obvious peaks corresponding to the vibration of Co-O are observed in the Raman shift between 400 and 600 cm⁻¹ when an applied potential of 1.1-1.8 V vs RHE is used, which demonstrate the CoFePBA/Co₂P electrode undergo reconstruction to give (Co, Fe)-OOH as active catalyst for the OER process. The bridging -CN- peaks in the range of 2000-2200 cm⁻¹ is maintained under all applied potentials... Moreover, the broad PO₄³⁻ peak is appeared in the range of 900-1100 cm⁻¹ when the potential reached 1.4 V vs RHE...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of N 1s and P 2p on fresh and spent CoFePBA/Co₂P shows C-N peak at 397.8 eV and P-O peak at ~135.0 eV, with signal weakening after test indicating partial dissolution of PO₄³⁻ and Fe(CN)₆³⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS peaks represent to C-N (397.8 eV) and P-O (≈135.0 eV) agree well with the result of in situ Raman (Figure 3b). And the weakening of the signal after test indicates partial dissolution of the PO₄³⁻ and Fe(CN)₆³⁻.

properties.description: XPS spectra showing N 1s and P 2p binding energy regions before and after test

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping of fresh and spent CoFePBA/Co₂P after activation at 200 mA/cm² shows decreased Fe(CN)₆³⁻/CN⁻ and greatly increased PO₄³⁻/PO₃⁻ with more uniform dispersion, confirming electrode reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, after activation in 20 wt% NaOH + satu. NaCl at 200 mA cm⁻², the concentration of Fe(CN)₆³⁻/CN⁻ decreased while PO₄³⁻/PO₃⁻ greatly increased (Figure 3c). And it is obvious that the dispersion of PO₄³⁻/PO₃⁻ becomes more uniform...

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronopotentiometry at 10 mA/cm² with EDTA-2Na addition shows CoFePBA/Co₂P has lowest ΔE = 6 mV, demonstrating strongest repulsion to negatively charged species compared to other electrodes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The smallest the change in E (lower ΔE), the weaker the electrode is nucleophilised, that is, more repulsive to EDTA²⁻, and also to Cl⁻. The Co(OH)₂ electrode, which does not produce an ionic layer, shows the highest ΔE = 21 mV. While the CoFePBA electrode (produces Fe(CN)₆³⁻ layer), and the Co₂P electrode (produces PO₄³⁻ layer), show lower ΔE of 10/13 mV... The lowest ΔE = 6 mV was achieved when CoFePBA/Co₂P electrode was used...

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronopotentiometry at 10 mA/cm² with EDTA-2Na addition shows CoFePBA/Co₂P has lowest ΔE = 6 mV, demonstrating strongest repulsion to negatively charged species compared to other electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy quantifies free Fe(CN)₆³⁻ in electrolyte after OER test, reaching concentrations of 21 ppm (30 min), 47 ppm (60 min), and 80 ppm (90 min) at the anode side.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV/Vis spectroscopy was employed for the qualitative and quantitative detection of free Fe(CN)₆³⁻ in the electrolyte after the long-term OER test... After the reaction for 30, 60, and 90 min... the concentration of Fe(CN)₆³⁻ (quantified by K₃Fe(CN)₆) in the electrolyte on the anode side reached 21, 47, and 80 ppm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ion Chromatography detects adsorbed Cl⁻ on different electrodes in 6 mM NaOH + 2.8 mM NaCl, showing CoFePBA/Co₂P has lowest Cl⁻ adhesion of 0.11 mM compared to Co₂P (0.17 mM), CoFePBA (0.18 mM), and Co(OH)₂ (0.43 mM).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, Ion Chromatography was used to detect the amount of adsorbed Cl⁻ species on different electrodes... the Cl⁻ adhesion amount decreases in the order of CoFePBA/Co₂P (0.11 mM) < Co₂P (0.17 mM) < CoFePBA (0.18 mM) < Co(OH)₂ (0.43 mM).

nodes.characterization_summary: Molecular dynamics simulations show CoFePBA/Co₂P reduces Cl⁻ concentration at 10.3 Å to 0.30 M, which is 5.5-fold lower than Co(OH)₂ (1.61 M) and lower than CoFePBA (0.58 M) and Co₂P (0.46 M), demonstrating synergistic repulsion effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Here, the [Cl⁻] at 10.3 Å is chosen for analysis (Figure 4c and Figure S23a), and the amount of Cl⁻ at this position for CoFePBA [Cl⁻] = 0.58 M and Co₂P electrodes [Cl⁻] = 0.46 M is 2.0 and 1.4 times higher than that of CoFePBA/Co₂P electrode [Cl⁻] = 0.30 M, respectively. It is worth noting that, [Cl⁻] of CoHO₂ at this position has reached 1.61 M, which is much higher than CoFePBA/CoP electrodes (5.5-fold).

nodes.characterization_summary: Molecular dynamics simulations show CoFePBA/Co₂P has excellent selective permeability with much higher [OH⁻] and much lower [Cl⁻] near the electrode surface compared to Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The [OH⁻] near CoFePBA/Co₂P surface is much higher than that near to Co(OH)₂, and [Cl⁻] is much lower. So the synergistic protective layer formed by PO₄³⁻ and Fe(CN)₆³⁻ has excellent selective permeability to OH⁻.
